new file mode 100644
index 0000000..2d15cb6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/terraform/variables.tf
@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+# ===============================
+# Required variables
+# ===============================
+variable "vultr_api_key" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "Api key for vultr (https://console.vultr.com/user/apiaccess/)"
+}
+variable "vultr_ssh_pub_key" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "Public key"
+}
+variable "vultr_region" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "Region to deploy the resources to"
+  default     = "lhr" # London
+}
+variable "vultr_plan_web" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "Plan for the web instance"
+  default     = "vc2-4c-8gb" # 8 vCPU | 32 GB RAM | 640 GB SSD
+}
+variable "vultr_plan_llm" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "Plan for the LLM instance"
+  default     = "vcg-a16-12c-120g-32vram" # 12 vCPU | 120 GB RAM | 700 GB SSD
+}
+variable "vultr_os_id" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "Id of the operating system"
+  default     = "2284" # Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x6
+}
+# ===============================
+# Terraform optional variables
+# ===============================
+variable "iac_ad_az_tenant_id" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "Id of the tenant who will deploy the resources on Azure. If null, the parameter will be read from the az cli configuration"
+  default     = null
+}
+variable "iac_ad_az_subscription_id" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "Id of the subscription used to deploy the resources on Azure. If null, the parameter will be read from the az cli configuration"
+  default     = null
+}
+variable "iac_ad_network_cidr" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "CIDR of the VPC to create. Meaning the range of IP addresses that will be available for the instances in the VPC."
+  default     = "192.168.0.0/16"
+  validation {
+    condition     = can(cidrnetmask(var.iac_ad_network_cidr))
+    error_message = "Must be a valid ip address with mask"
+  }
+}
+variable "iac_ad_router_subnet_cidr" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "CIDR of the subnet to create for the router. Meaning the range of IP addresses that will be available for the instances in the subnet."
+  default     = "192.168.0.0/24"
+  validation {
+    condition     = can(cidrnetmask(var.iac_ad_router_subnet_cidr))
+    error_message = "Must be a valid ip address with mask"
+  }
+}
+variable "iac_ad_server_subnet_cidr" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "CIDR of the subnet to create for the game system. Meaning the range of IP addresses that will be available for the instances in the subnet."
+  default     = "192.168.1.0/24"
+  validation {
+    condition     = can(cidrnetmask(var.iac_ad_server_subnet_cidr))
+    error_message = "Must be a valid ip address with mask"
+  }
+}
+variable "iac_ad_vulnbox_subnet_cidr" {
+  type        = string
+  description = "CIDR of the subnet to create for the vulnboxes. Meaning the range of IP addresses that will be available for the instances in the subnet."
+  default     = "192.168.2.0/24"
+  validation {
+    condition     = can(cidrnetmask(var.iac_ad_vulnbox_subnet_cidr))
+    error_message = "Must be a valid ip address with mask"
+  }
+}
+variable "iac_ad_vulnbox_count" {
+  description = "Number of vulnboxes to create"
+  type        = number
+  default     = 1
+  validation {
+    condition     = var.iac_ad_vulnbox_count > 0 && var.iac_ad_vulnbox_count <= 250
+    error_message = "The number of vulnboxes must be greater than 0 and no more than 250"
+  }
+}
+variable "iac_ad_wireguard_port" {
+  description = "Port to use for the wireguard VPN"
+  type        = number
+  default     = 51820
+  validation {
+    condition     = var.iac_ad_wireguard_port >= 80 && var.iac_ad_wireguard_port <= 65535
+    error_message = "The wireguard port must be between 80 and 65535"
+  }
+}
+variable "iac_ad_server_ports" {
+  description = "Ports to open on the game system"
+  type        = set(number)
+  default     = [80, 443]
+
+  validation {
+    condition     = length(var.iac_ad_server_ports) > 0
+    error_message = "At least one port must be specified"
+  }
+
+  validation {
+    condition     = alltrue([for port in var.iac_ad_server_ports : port >= 20 && port <= 65535])
+    error_message = "Ports must be between 20 and 65535"
+  }
+}
diff --git a/terraform/vultr.tf b/terraform/vultr.tf
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a4ac29f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/terraform/vultr.tf
@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+terraform {
+  required_providers {
+    vultr = {
+      source  = "vultr/vultr"
+      version = "2.33.2"
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+# Configure the Vultr Provider
+provider "vultr" {
+  api_key     = var.vultr_api_key
+  rate_limit  = 100
+  retry_limit = 3
+}
+
+resource "vultr_vpc" "vpc" {
+  description    = "HackTheBurgh2026VPC"
+  region         = var.vultr_region
+  v4_subnet      = "10.0.0.0"
+  v4_subnet_mask = 24
+}
+
+resource "vultr_ssh_key" "ssh_key" {
+  name    = "HackTheBurgh2026Key"
+  ssh_key = REDACTED
+}
+
+resource "vultr_firewall_group" "firewall_web" {
+  description = "Firewall for the web instance"
+}
+
+resource "vultr_firewall_rule" "allow_22" {
+  firewall_group_id = vultr_firewall_group.firewall_web.id
+  protocol          = "tcp"
+  ip_type           = "v4"
+  subnet            = "0.0.0.0"
+  subnet_size       = 0
+  port              = "22"
+  notes             = "Allow SSH"
+}
+
+resource "vultr_firewall_rule" "allow_80" {
+  firewall_group_id = vultr_firewall_group.firewall_web.id
+  protocol          = "tcp"
+  ip_type           = "v4"
+  subnet            = "0.0.0.0"
+  subnet_size       = 0
+  port              = "80"
+  notes             = "Allow HTTP"
+}
+
+resource "vultr_firewall_rule" "allow_443" {
+  firewall_group_id = vultr_firewall_group.firewall_web.id
+  protocol          = "tcp"
+  ip_type           = "v4"
+  subnet            = "0.0.0.0"
+  subnet_size       = 0
+  port              = "443"
+  notes             = "Allow HTTPs"
+}
+
+resource "vultr_instance" "web" {
+  plan                = var.vultr_plan_web
+  region              = var.vultr_region
+  os_id               = var.vultr_os_id
+  label               = "HackTheBurgh2026VPS"
+  tags                = ["HackTheBurgh2026"]
+  firewall_group_id   = vultr_firewall_group.firewall_web.id
+  enable_ipv6         = false
+  disable_public_ipv4 = false
+  vpc_ids             = [vultr_vpc.vpc.id]
+  backups             = "disabled"
+  user_scheme         = "limited"
+  ssh_key_ids      = [vultr_ssh_key.ssh_key.id]
+  ddos_protection  = true
+  activation_email = false
+}
+
+resource "vultr_firewall_group" "firewall_llm" {
+  description = "Firewall for the LLM instance"
+}
+
+resource "vultr_firewall_rule" "allow_11434" {
+  firewall_group_id = vultr_firewall_group.firewall_web.id
+  protocol          = "tcp"
+  ip_type           = "v4"
+  subnet            = vultr_vpc.vpc.v4_subnet
+  subnet_size       = 8
+  port              = "11434"
+  notes             = "Allow olama"
+}
+
+resource "vultr_instance" "llm" {
+  plan                = var.vultr_plan_llm
+  region              = var.vultr_region
+  os_id               = var.vultr_os_id
+  label               = "HackTheBurgh2026VPS"
+  tags                = ["HackTheBurgh2026"]
+  firewall_group_id   = vultr_firewall_group.firewall_llm.id
+  enable_ipv6         = false
+  vpc_ids             = [vultr_vpc.vpc.id]

content.text:
PR #8 is "feat: add terraform for vultr" by TendTo (Ernesto). It adds 609 lines across 8 files, all new and all under `terraform/` plus `.gitignore`. It touches no app code and doesn't conflict with main.

**What it does**

It describes the Vultr cloud setup as Terraform code, so the servers can be created or torn down with one command instead of clicking through the Vultr console:
- **A private network** (VPC 10.0.0.0/24) in London.
- **A web server**: Ubuntu 24.04, 4 vCPU and 8 GB RAM. Its firewall opens 22, 80 and 443.
- **An LLM server**: an A16 GPU box with 12 vCPU, 120 GB RAM and 32 GB VRAM. It has no public IP and is reachable only over the private network, presumably to run Ollama/Gemma for the `ai/ollama.py` provider.
- **A firewall rule for Ollama's port 11434**, limited to the private network.
- `terraform/deploy.sh`, which runs `terraform apply` and prints the web server's IP.

**Problems I'd raise before merging**

1. **It commits Terraform state files, and one leaks a secret.**
   - `terraform.tfstate.backup` contains the web instance's root `default_password` (in plain text) and a Vultr web-console (KVM) link. That instance is 209.250.224.55. It isn't our prod server (prod is 78.141.206.107), and the current `terraform.tfstate` has no resources, so it looks like that instance was already destroyed. Even so, the password and console link shouldn't be in git history.
   - State files belong in `.gitignore` (`*.tfstate*`), not in the repo.
2. **The Ollama rule is on the wrong firewall.** `allow_11434` is attached to `firewall_web` instead of `firewall_llm`, so the LLM box's own firewall has no rules. Its source is also 10.0.0.0/8 rather than the VPC's /24.
3. **Some variables are left over from another project.** All the `iac_ad_*` variables (Azure tenant, vulnboxes, WireGuard, "game system") are unused. They look like they came from an attack-defence CTF template.
4. **Small mistakes:**
   - The plan comments are wrong: `vc2-4c-8gb` is 4 vCPU and 8 GB, not "8 vCPU | 32 GB".
   - Both instances share the label `HackTheBurgh2026VPS`.
   - `deploy.sh` runs `terraform output vultr_instance.web.main_ip`, which won't work because no `output` block is defined.
   - There's no `vultr_ssh_pub_key` in the tfvars example.
5. **Cost.** A GPU A16 instance is expensive per hour, so `terraform apply` with the defaults spins one up.

**Bottom line:** the app is unaffected, so merging is low-risk for prod, but I wouldn't merge it as-is. I'd ask TendTo to delete the two state files and ignore `*.tfstate*`, move the 11434 rule to `firewall_llm`, and drop the unused variables. I can make those fixes on the branch or leave a review comment on the PR, whichever you prefer.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploy Earwitness to a fresh Ubuntu server over SSH (password auth).
#
#   bash scripts/deploy.sh [user@host]                      # with the deploy key
#   SSHPASS='server-password' bash scripts/deploy.sh         # first time, no key yet
#
# A password is only read from $SSHPASS (for SSH and sudo) and never written
# to disk. With the key, sudo must be passwordless on the server. Re-running the script updates the code
# and restarts the service.
set -euo pipefail

TARGET="${1:-linuxuser@78.141.206.107}"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
KEY="${DEPLOY_KEY:-$HOME/.ssh/earwitness_deploy}"

# Prefer the deploy key (no password needed); fall back to SSHPASS.
if [[ -f "$KEY" ]] && ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 -i "$KEY" "$TARGET" true 2>/dev/null; then
  SSH_OPTS=(-o BatchMode=yes -i "$KEY")
  RUN=()
  SUDO_LINE=""
elif [[ -n "${SSHPASS:-}" ]]; then
  command -v sshpass >/dev/null || brew install hudochenkov/sshpass/sshpass
  SSH_OPTS=(-o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -o PreferredAuthentications=password)
  RUN=(sshpass -e)
  SUDO_LINE="$SSHPASS"
else
  echo "No working deploy key ($KEY) and no SSHPASS set." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "==> Copying code to $TARGET:~/earwitness"
${RUN[@]+"${RUN[@]}"} rsync -az --delete \
  -e "ssh ${SSH_OPTS[*]}" \
  --exclude .venv --exclude web/node_modules --exclude web/dist --exclude web/dist-stable \
  --exclude cases --exclude __pycache__ --exclude .pytest_cache --exclude .ruff_cache \
  --exclude .git --exclude .DS_Store --exclude .env --exclude ".env.bak-*" \
  "$ROOT/" "$TARGET:earwitness/"

echo "==> Setting up the server (this takes a few minutes the first time)"
# bash -s reads its script from stdin line by line: the first line reads the
# next line (the sudo password) into a variable, then the setup script follows.
{ printf 'read -r SUDO_PASS\n%s\n' "$SUDO_LINE"; cat "$ROOT/scripts/remote_setup.sh"; } |
  ${RUN[@]+"${RUN[@]}"} ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$TARGET" 'bash -s'

HOST="${TARGET#*@}"
echo "==> Done: http://$HOST/"

content.text:
I've backed up prod onto the prod server itself, in `/home/linuxuser/backups/earwitness-20261108-063022Z/` (2.3 GB, with 409 GB still free on the disk). The folder is readable only by `linuxuser`.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `db.dump` | The whole Tiger Cloud Postgres database in `pg_dump` custom format, including the grid-frequency record. Restore it with `pg_restore`. |
| `db.sql.gz` | The same dump as plain SQL, readable with `zcat`. |
| `earwitness-files.tar.gz` | All of `~/earwitness` (155 MB of `media`, `demo` and the code) minus `.venv` and `node_modules`. That covers all 74 cases in `cases/`: uploads, events, artifacts and `case.json` with owners and history. |
| `env` | A copy of `.env`, which holds the secrets, hence the private permissions. |
| `earwitness.service`, `nginx.tar.gz` | The systemd unit and nginx config. |
| `SHA256SUMS` | Checksums for the files above. |

**Checks:**
- The dump has 112 rows in `earwitness.cases`, the same as the live database.
- The archive contains all 74 `case.json` files.
- `pg_dump` printed one warning, about a circular foreign key in TimescaleDB's own `continuous_agg` table. TimescaleDB dumps always print this. If a restore ever hits it, run `timescaledb_pre_restore()` and `timescaledb_post_restore()` around it.
- The database has more case rows (112) than there are case folders (74). I'd guess deleted cases leave their database row behind, but I haven't checked.

**To make the backup I installed `postgresql-client-18` on the server.** No `pg_dump` was installed there, and it had to match the database's Postgres 18.

The backup sits on the same machine and disk as prod, so it protects against a bad deploy or deletion but not against losing the server. Copying it off with `scp` or Vultr snapshots would cover that. I can also make this a nightly cron job.

=== #10
## Summary
Scrolling over the case map now zooms it, like the globe.

- **Before:**
  - Scroll zoom was switched off on the Leaflet map, so scrolling over it did nothing.
  - Leaflet's built-in scroll zoom wasn't a usable fix: it drops wheel events while its zoom animation runs, so trackpad scrolling barely registered (40 trackpad-style events zoomed about 6%).
- **Now:** a native wheel handler (`passive: false`) zooms at once, in proportion to the scroll, around the point under the pointer.
  - Fractional zoom: a mouse notch is about half a level, and a trackpad zooms smoothly.
  - The page doesn't scroll while the pointer is over the map.
- **No blank frames:** the zoom moves the view the way Leaflet's pinch zoom does. A "pinch" move keeps the current tiles on screen, scaled, instead of resetting the view and throwing them away. The gesture ends 150 ms after the last wheel event, and then sharper tiles load.

Dragging, the +/− buttons and the Street/Satellite switch are unchanged. The small static map in the reveal panel stays frozen on purpose.

## Testing
- **Headless Chrome:**
  - Trackpad-style scrolling zooms in (level 7 → about 8.6) and mouse notches zoom back out.
  - Mid-scroll, tiles cover the whole map throughout (checked with a screenshot taken mid-gesture).
  - The page stays put over the map and scrolls normally beside it.
- **Headless Firefox 159:** the same zoom-in/out and page checks.
- `npm run build` (tsc + vite) passes.

Uses two internal Leaflet methods (`_move`, `_moveEnd`), the same ones its pinch zoom uses. They are typed locally in `MapView.tsx`.

=== #9
## Summary
More WebGPU work on top of #7, now **running automatically** and feeding the case page. When a case opens in a browser with WebGPU, the viewer's GPU starts its own checks right away and gives first answers in seconds, while the server's checks take minutes. The server's findings remain the official record; browser results are labelled as found in your browser.

Includes `main` as of `79d9ac4` (live analysis panel, feed search, compact location panel). The merge needed one CSS conflict resolved, keeping both sides.

### Automatic browser checks, in the normal case flow (`lib/gpuChecks.tsx`)
- **What runs:**
  - **Videos:** frame scan (every frame up to a minute, 2× up to ten minutes, longer only on request), mains hum (the steadier of the 45–65 / 95–125 Hz traces, mapped to a 50/60 Hz grid), and a steady high tone (15 kHz–top).
  - **Photos:** the JPEG ghost.
- **No separate panels.** `browserLayer()` expresses the results the way the server does, so they show up where people already look:
  - **Findings list:** cuts, stretches of repeated frames (flagged as frame-rate conversion when regular), "Lights on a 50 Hz grid", the steady hum, high tones, the photo's save quality and odd-quality areas.
  - **Key moments:** cuts and repeated-frame stretches.
  - **Photo viewer:** odd-quality areas as flagged regions, using the findings' boxes.
  - **Exhibits by topic:**
    - *Frame-by-frame change* under Timeline;
    - *Lamp flicker map* under Light;
    - *Transcribe on this device* under Text & speech, when the server has no transcript.
  - **Live analysis panel:** the browser checks' progress while the case runs.
- **Labelling:** they appear as checks named "… (your browser)", with a note that they are measured in the browser and not saved with the case.
- **Verdict:** it and its counts still read the server's state only; the same case shows the same verdict with or without WebGPU.

### Photo tools
- **JPEG ghost lens:** for each 8×8 block, the quality it was last saved at (39 candidates, best fit on the block's luma DCT). Blocks agreeing with the picture's dominant quality are dimmed; the rest are coloured, with a legend. The code is shared as `lib/ghost.ts`.
- **Find copies** (button / **C**): select an area and the whole picture is searched by normalised cross-correlation. The search works on a scaled, slightly blurred greyscale copy, so matches survive sub-pixel offsets. Matches are drawn as boxes with their scores.

### Audio and video tools
- **Live spectrogram** ("Live" on each spectrogram): a Hann-windowed DFT on the GPU for any band and window, with real dBFS and a strongest-frequency trace. The 3D view uses it, so heights are real decibels.
- **Frame scan** (panel under the player):
  - **Change curve:** frame-to-frame change, with abrupt changes and exact repeats marked.
  - **Lamp-flicker map:** per-pixel flicker at the aliased 100/120 Hz frequencies, averaged along rows and compared with a control frequency (the noise floor).
  - **Source:** reads the original file when the browser can play it.
  - **Firefox:** frames reach the GPU through a canvas, because Firefox's WebGPU won't copy from a `<video>`.
- **Multi-frame zoom** ("Stack on your GPU" in the video zoom dialog): up to 32 frames, aligned to the sub-pixel and averaged. Frames where the region changed are left out rather than smeared in.
- **Transcript on your device** (experimental): Whisper tiny or base on WebGPU via `@huggingface/transformers` **4.3.1** (pinned), loaded only when you click Transcribe.

### Fixes along the way
- **`useGpuCanvas`:** it now sets up canvases that mount after the GPU device is ready. Before this, such canvases stayed blank.
- **Not tested:** the browser checks' rows in the live analysis panel while a case is running (all test cases had already finished).
- **Frame scan:**
  - It now reads the first frame (it used to read 899 of 900).
  - A run of repeated frames no longer makes ordinary frames count as abrupt changes.

## Testing
All in headless Chrome with real WebGPU (Apple M3), clean console unless noted. The automatic checks ran with no clicks.

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `demo/01_planted.mp4` | Browser findings: **abrupt change at 20.00 s** (also in the server's 0:20 key moment), **steady 18.50 kHz tone**, no lamp flicker; exhibits under Timeline, Light and Text & speech. The verdict and counts are identical with WebGPU off. |
| Clip re-timed 25→30 fps | **64 repeated frames**, the exact count from per-frame checksums; no false cuts; one finding and one Key-moments entry. |
| `demo/04_lamps_50hz.mp4` | Finding **"Lights on a 50 Hz grid (flicker 53× the noise)"** (a CPU check gives 45×; a clip without lamps gives 0.6×). |
| `demo/07_hum/spliced.mp4` | **Steady hum at 100.05 Hz → 50 Hz grid**; a CPU FFT agrees the hum sits at 100/150 Hz. |
| `demo/photos/11_edited.jpg` | Ghost: **Q92**, matching the file's real quantisation table. ELA shows the Q45 paste (3.3 vs 14.1 brightness). Find copies finds the copy-move at (459, 880) with 89%. |
| Speech clip (macOS `say`) | Whisper tiny transcribes it in 9.9 s, including the model download. |
| Firefox video restriction (simulated) | The automatic frame scan reads 360/360 frames through the canvas, with the same result. |
| No WebGPU | No browser findings, exhibits, lenses or switches; pages unchanged. |

Earlier features (lenses, live and 3D spectrograms, globe, particles) were re-checked after the `useGpuCanvas` change.

`npm run build` (tsc + vite) passes; `uv run pytest`: 71 passed, 1 skipped.

## Limits
- **JPEG ghost:** it boxes only areas that still carry texture. The demo's Q45 paste is perfectly flat, so the ghost has no evidence there. ELA shows that paste instead.
- **Frame scan:**
  - Exact repeats survive only in the original file. When the browser can't play the original (e.g. HEVC on some systems), the scan falls back to the re-encoded copy, where repeats may not show.
  - A 5-minute clip scans at 2×, which takes about 2.5 minutes.
- **Transcript on your device:** Whisper tiny is rough on names. The first use downloads the model (~40–80 MB) and a 27 MB WebAssembly runtime.
- **Firefox:** not tested in a real browser; headless Firefox has no WebGPU adapter. Its video restriction was simulated in Chrome.

content.text:
I merged and deployed both of Denis's new PRs. The server's health check passed, and the live site is serving the same bundle my local build produced.

- **#10, scroll to zoom on the map:** scrolling over the case map now zooms it, as the globe does.
- **#9, automatic checks in the browser:** when someone opens a case in a browser with WebGPU, their own GPU runs quick checks straight away. For videos that's cuts, repeated frames, lamp flicker, mains hum and high tones; for photos it's the JPEG ghost. The results appear in the normal findings and exhibits, labelled "(your browser)", and they're not saved with the case. The verdict still comes only from the server. It also adds new tools: Find copies, a live spectrogram, multi-frame zoom and a transcript made on the device.

Both merged without conflicts and the web build passes. I didn't run the Python tests, since neither PR touches the backend.

Things to know:
- **Scrolling gets captured.** While the pointer is over the map, it zooms the map instead of scrolling the page. On the case page the location map is large, so someone scrolling down could get stuck zooming. If that's annoying, a "hold ⌘ to zoom" rule is an easy change.
- **Large download.** #9 adds the Whisper transcription runtime, with a 27 MB file. It only downloads when someone clicks Transcribe, but the deploy is now heavier.
- **More GPU work per visit.** The browser checks start on every case open. A long video scans for a couple of minutes on the visitor's GPU.

I left the Terraform PR (#8) open because of the problems I raised earlier.

Design an "Effort" setting, where we can have more complex processing on request, or lighter one. The current level should be considered "medium". Add more things for the higher effort ones (we can tolerate longer waiting times) eg stars/sun and anything else you can think of. Screenshots should still attempt to run these. Low effort should be quicker. Effort level should be recorded with each case (and changable during re-calculations). Be creative with your methods, right now we don't do well in rural areas on areas with no text! If you want a free api to use, tell and i can prob register for you

7	   language and the transcript, what an AI listener heard (accents, sirens,

"""The ordered list of analysis modules the case runner executes, per media kind."""

import importlib
from typing import Any

_VIDEO_MODULES = [
    ("earwitness.modules.provenance", "Provenance"),
    ("earwitness.modules.timeline", "Timeline"),
    ("earwitness.modules.spectrum", "Spectrum"),
    ("earwitness.modules.enf", "Enf"),
    ("earwitness.modules.light", "Light"),
    ("earwitness.modules.pulse", "Pulse"),
    ("earwitness.modules.tamper", "Tamper"),
    ("earwitness.modules.avsync", "AvSync"),
    ("earwitness.modules.ocr", "Ocr"),
    ("earwitness.modules.transcript", "Transcript"),
    ("earwitness.modules.sounds", "Sounds"),
    ("earwitness.modules.vision", "Vision"),
    ("earwitness.modules.geo", "Geo"),
    ("earwitness.modules.weather", "Weather"),
    ("earwitness.modules.brief", "Brief"),
]

# Still photographs: no clock, no sound, but every pixel and every byte of
# metadata at full resolution.
_IMAGE_MODULES = [
    ("earwitness.modules.photo_provenance", "PhotoProvenance"),
    ("earwitness.modules.compression", "Compression"),
    ("earwitness.modules.photo_pixels", "PhotoPixels"),
    ("earwitness.modules.hidden", "Hidden"),
    ("earwitness.modules.faces", "Faces"),
    ("earwitness.modules.synthetic", "Synthetic"),
    ("earwitness.modules.ocr", "Ocr"),
    ("earwitness.modules.vision", "Vision"),
    ("earwitness.modules.geo", "Geo"),
    ("earwitness.modules.weather", "Weather"),
    ("earwitness.modules.brief", "Brief"),
]

_BY_KIND = {"video": _VIDEO_MODULES, "image": _IMAGE_MODULES, "audio": _VIDEO_MODULES}


def all_modules(kind: str = "video") -> list[Any]:
    modules = []

    for path, cls in _BY_KIND.get(kind, _VIDEO_MODULES):
        try:
            module = importlib.import_module(path)
        except ModuleNotFoundError as error:
            if error.name == path:
                continue

            raise

        modules.append(getattr(module, cls)())

    return modules


def kinds() -> list[str]:
    return ["video", "image"]

# Effort levels (Quick / Standard / Deep) and deeper geolocation

## Context
Geolocation is the selling point, but it struggles in rural scenes with no text or landmarks. Today the pipeline is: 6 frames → geo-sleuth crops → one proposal → Wikipedia photo + one satellite tile → verify. It has nothing to check a field, a lane or a moor against.

The user wants an **effort** setting:
- **low:** quicker.
- **medium:** exactly today's behaviour.
- **high:** slower but uses many more methods (sun, stars and more).

The effort is stored with each case and can be changed on rerun.

From the prod logs (median module time, 71 video cases):
- geo 181 s (max 447)
- brief 19 s
- vision 16 s
- everything else ≤ 8 s

So effort is mostly about geo.

## 1. Plumbing (backend)
- **Option.** `options["effort"]` ∈ `low|medium|high`, default `medium`.
  - Validated by a new `_effort()` in `server/app.py`, next to `_ai_provider()`.
  - Upload: `POST /api/cases?effort=`.
  - Rerun: `POST /rerun?effort=` saves the new value, as `ai_provider` does today (`app.py:258`).
  - The history entries `uploaded` and `reran` both record `effort=…` (`Case.record`).
- **Exposure.** `Case.summary()` (`jobs.py:100`) and the `case` event (`jobs.py:456`) include `effort`. Mirror it in `web/src/lib/types.ts` (`CaseInfo`, `CaseSummary`, `CustodyEntry`) and `docs/PROTOCOL.md`.
- **Context helper.** `CaseContext.effort` property plus `ctx.by_effort(low=…, medium=…, high=…)` in `modules/base.py`, so modules read their knobs in one line.
- **Module gating.** Optional class attribute `min_effort = "high"`. `run_case` marks such a module `skipped` ("Runs at Deep effort") and publishes `None`, reusing the path for unscheduled modules so `wait_for` never hangs.
- **AI calls.**
  - Geo already passes `effort="high"`; low uses `"low"`.
  - Brief and vision pass `ctx.by_effort(low="low")` (None otherwise = today's default).
  - The AI cache key already includes effort and content, so a rerun at another level never reuses stale answers.

## 2. What each level does in geo

| | low (Quick, ~1 min) | medium (today) | high (Deep, ~5–10 min) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frames (video) | 3 | 6 | 10, plus quarter crops of the 2 sharpest |
| geo-sleuth intake | off | 2 frames | 4 frames |
| Clue inventory pass | – | – | yes (§3a) |
| Proposals | 1 pass, 3 candidates, AI effort low | 1 pass, 4 candidates | 3 independent passes on different frame subsets, clustered (§3b) |
| References | satellite only | Wikipedia + satellite | + multi-zoom satellite, Commons/Mapillary ground photos, terrain skyline, OSM features, sun, weather (§3c–h) |
| Verify | effort low | as now | as now + one coarse-to-fine refinement round (§3i) |

Other modules:
- `pulse` gets `min_effort="medium"`, so low skips it.
- At high, `sounds` also asks for bird and wildlife species and farm or rural sounds; this is a prompt addition and the output feeds geo's clues.

## 3. New Deep methods
New file `src/earwitness/modules/geo_deep.py` holds pure, testable helpers, with network calls behind small functions that tests can patch. Each method returns one or both of:
- **Per-candidate scores**, which flow into the verifier's prompt and into the final rescoring.
- **Constraints**: a `ring` (centre, radius, width) or a `band` (lat/lon range). These are drawn on the map and passed to the proposer and refiner as text.

"""Sound sleuth: what an expert ear would pick out of the background.

An audio-capable model listens to the soundtrack and lists what it hears:
sirens (their pattern differs by country), announcements, birds, traffic,
church bells, languages and accents, crowd size, indoor or outdoor. Each item
is a clue to where and when the recording was made. Everything here is

    '{"environment": "one sentence: indoor/outdoor, size, setting",'

    "health or other sensitive traits."
)

            raise Skip("could not extract audio")

"""Extra geolocation methods for Deep-effort runs.

The standard pipeline (``geo.py``) proposes places and checks them against a
Wikipedia photo and one satellite tile, which works where there is a landmark
or text. The countryside has neither, so a Deep run adds checks that work on
fields, lanes, hills and skies:

* a clue inventory: what a GeoGuessr player reads in a rural scene (poles,
  road lines, walls, crops, soil, terrain), plus sun, shadows and stars;
* several independent proposals, clustered: agreement is evidence;
* ground-level photos near each candidate (Wikimedia Commons, Mapillary);
* OpenStreetMap: do the features seen (wind turbines, pylons, coast) exist there?
* terrain: does the skyline in the frame match the horizon rendered from the
  elevation model at the candidate?
* the sun: with a trustworthy time, its height above the horizon puts the
  camera on a ring around the point where the sun was overhead;
* stars: a plate-solved star field bounds the latitude;
* weather: rain in the frame and a dry record there (or the reverse) counts
  against a candidate.

Every function here either returns None (could not check) or a result that
states what it measured. Network calls are small functions so tests can patch
them; the pure maths (rings, horizons, clustering) is tested directly.
"""

import asyncio
import math
import os
from datetime import datetime
from datetime import timezone
from typing import Any

import cv2
import httpx
import numpy as np

EARTH_KM = 6371.0
_KM_PER_DEG = 111.195
_USER_AGENT = "earwitness-forensics/0.2 (hackathon research demo)"

# ---- clue inventory ----------------------------------------------------------------

# OpenStreetMap features a frame can show, with the tags that mark them and
# how far away they could plausibly be while still visible (metres).
FEATURES: dict[str, tuple[list[str], int]] = {
    "wind_turbine": (['node["generator:source"="wind"]'], 12000),
    "power_line": (['way["power"="line"]'], 3000),
    "railway": (['way["railway"="rail"]'], 2000),
    "motorway": (['way["highway"="motorway"]'], 2000),
    "river": (['way["waterway"="river"]'], 3000),
    "lake": (['way["natural"="water"]', 'relation["natural"="water"]'], 4000),
    "coastline": (['way["natural"="coastline"]'], 10000),
    "church": (['node["amenity"="place_of_worship"]', 'way["amenity"="place_of_worship"]'], 3000),
    "lighthouse": (['node["man_made"="lighthouse"]', 'way["man_made"="lighthouse"]'], 15000),
    "castle": (['node["historic"="castle"]', 'way["historic"="castle"]'], 5000),
    "mountain_peak": (['node["natural"="peak"]'], 20000),
    "vineyard": (['way["landuse"="vineyard"]'], 2000),
    "forest": (['way["landuse"="forest"]', 'way["natural"="wood"]'], 1500),
    "golf_course": (['way["leisure"="golf_course"]'], 1500),
}  # fmt: skip
_FEATURE_WORDS = {
    "wind_turbine": "wind turbines", "power_line": "high-voltage power lines", "railway": "a railway",
    "motorway": "a motorway", "river": "a river", "lake": "a lake", "coastline": "the sea coast",
    "church": "a church", "lighthouse": "a lighthouse", "castle": "a castle",
    "mountain_peak": "mountain peaks", "vineyard": "vineyards", "forest": "woodland",
    "golf_course": "a golf course",
}  # fmt: skip

INVENTORY_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "additionalProperties": False,
    "required": [
        "scene_type", "driving_side", "road", "poles_and_wires", "roadside", "boundaries",
        "land_use", "vegetation", "soil_and_rock", "terrain", "horizon", "buildings",
        "vehicles", "osm_features", "lighting", "sun_visible", "sun_elevation_deg",
        "sun_basis", "shadow_direction", "hemisphere_hint", "hemisphere_reasoning",
        "stars_visible", "constellations", "camera_tilt_deg", "moon", "strongest_clues",
    ],
    "properties": {
        "scene_type": {"type": "string", "enum": ["urban", "suburban", "rural", "wilderness", "indoor", "water"]},
        "driving_side": {"type": "string", "enum": ["left", "right", "unknown"]},
        "road": {"type": "string", "description": "Surface, width, centre and edge line colours and pattern; 'none' if no road."},
        "poles_and_wires": {"type": "string", "description": "Utility pole material and shape, cross-arms, insulators, wires; 'none'."},
        "roadside": {"type": "string", "description": "Bollards (shape, colour, reflectors), guard rails, kerbs, sign shapes and colours even if unreadable."},
        "boundaries": {"type": "string", "description": "Fences, dry-stone walls, hedgerows, gates."},
        "land_use": {"type": "string", "description": "Fields and their shapes, crops, livestock, orchards, vineyards, forestry."},
        "vegetation": {"type": "string", "description": "Tree and plant species or families, season."},
        "soil_and_rock": {"type": "string", "description": "Soil colour, exposed rock type."},
        "terrain": {"type": "string", "description": "Flat, rolling, hilly, mountainous; valley, moor, plateau."},
        "horizon": {"type": "string", "enum": ["natural_hills", "mountains", "natural_flat", "sea", "buildings", "trees", "none"],
                    "description": "What forms the skyline across most of the frame."},
        "buildings": {"type": "string", "description": "Roof material and colour, wall material, style; 'none'."},
        "vehicles": {"type": "string", "description": "Makes, plate shapes and colours, farm machinery; 'none'."},
        "osm_features": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "enum": list(FEATURES)},
                         "description": "Only features clearly visible in the frames."},
        "lighting": {"type": "string", "enum": ["day", "twilight", "night", "indoor", "unknown"]},
        "sun_visible": {"type": "boolean", "description": "The sun itself, or sharp shadows that show where it is."},
        "sun_elevation_deg": {"type": ["number", "null"],
                              "description": "Sun height above the horizon in degrees, estimated from a vertical object and its shadow (elevation = atan(height / shadow length)) or from the sun's position in the frame; null if it cannot be judged."},
        "sun_basis": {"type": "string", "description": "What the elevation estimate rests on."},
        "shadow_direction": {"type": "string", "description": "Which way shadows fall in the frame; 'none'."},
        "hemisphere_hint": {"type": "string", "enum": ["north", "south", "unknown"]},
        "hemisphere_reasoning": {"type": "string"},
        "stars_visible": {"type": "boolean"},
        "constellations": {"type": "string", "description": "Constellations or bright stars you can identify; 'none'."},
        "camera_tilt_deg": {"type": ["number", "null"], "description": "How far above level the camera points (0 level, 90 straight up); null if unknown."},
        "moon": {"type": "string", "description": "Moon phase and position if visible; 'none'."},
        "strongest_clues": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "maxItems": 6},
    },
}  # fmt: skip

INVENTORY = (
    "You are a top GeoGuessr player and open-source geolocation analyst. Do NOT guess the place "
    "yet. Make an exact inventory of every location clue in these frames, especially the ones "
    "that work where there is no text and no landmark: utility poles, road line colours, "
    "bollards, guard rails, walls and hedges, field shapes, crops, livestock, soil colour, tree "
    "species, terrain, the skyline, roofs, the sun and shadows, stars. Describe only what you can "
    "see; write 'none' or 'unknown' rather than inventing. Estimate the sun's elevation only from "
    "a real measurement (a vertical object and its shadow, or the sun in frame)."
)

REFINE = (
    "You are a world-class geolocation analyst refining an earlier answer. The earlier passes put "
    "this footage near the region given below, but no exact spot was confirmed. You see the "
    "evidence frames, the clue inventory, the automatic checks, and satellite views of the region "
    "at two scales. Propose 3-5 EXACT spots inside or near that region (each with a radius of at "
    "most 3 km) where the frames could have been taken: match field patterns, road shapes, "
    "rivers, woods, slopes and settlements in the satellite views to the frames. Use real "
    "coordinates of real places; name the nearest village or road in 'place'."
)


def inventory_text(inv: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """The inventory as lines for the proposer's clue block."""
    keys = [
        ("scene_type", "Scene"), ("driving_side", "Driving side"), ("road", "Road"),
        ("poles_and_wires", "Poles and wires"), ("roadside", "Roadside furniture"),
        ("boundaries", "Field boundaries"), ("land_use", "Land use"), ("vegetation", "Vegetation"),
        ("soil_and_rock", "Soil and rock"), ("terrain", "Terrain"), ("horizon", "Skyline"),
        ("buildings", "Buildings"), ("vehicles", "Vehicles"), ("shadow_direction", "Shadows"),
        ("constellations", "Stars"), ("moon", "Moon"),
    ]  # fmt: skip
    lines = [
        f"{label}: {inv[key]}"
        for key, label in keys
        if str(inv.get(key) or "").strip().lower() not in ("", "none", "unknown")
    ]

    if inv.get("hemisphere_hint") in ("north", "south"):
        lines.append(
            f"Hemisphere hint: {inv['hemisphere_hint']} ({inv.get('hemisphere_reasoning', '')})"
        )

    if inv.get("strongest_clues"):
        lines.append("Strongest clues: " + "; ".join(inv["strongest_clues"]))

    return "\n".join(lines)


# ---- ensemble ----------------------------------------------------------------------


def haversine_km(a: tuple[float, float], b: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
    lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2 = map(math.radians, (*a, *b))
    h = (
        math.sin((lat2 - lat1) / 2) ** 2
        + math.cos(lat1) * math.cos(lat2) * math.sin((lon2 - lon1) / 2) ** 2
    )

    return 2 * EARTH_KM * math.asin(math.sqrt(min(1.0, h)))


def cluster(
    passes: list[list[dict[str, Any]]], within_km: float = 25.0, keep: int = 5
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Merge candidates from independent proposal passes.

    Candidates within ``within_km`` of each other are one place. Each merged
    candidate keeps the most probable member's text and coordinates, its
    probability becomes the mean over all passes (a pass that missed it adds
    0), and ``votes`` counts the passes that proposed it.
    """
    groups: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    flat = sorted(
        ((p, c) for p, cands in enumerate(passes) for c in cands),
        key=lambda pc: -float(pc[1].get("probability") or 0),
    )

    for pass_index, candidate in flat:
        here = (float(candidate["latitude"]), float(candidate["longitude"]))
        group = next(
            (
                g for g in groups
                if haversine_km(here, (g["lead"]["latitude"], g["lead"]["longitude"])) <= within_km
            ),
            None,
        )  # fmt: skip

        if group is None:
            groups.append({"lead": candidate, "passes": {pass_index}, "total": 0.0})
            group = groups[-1]

        group["passes"].add(pass_index)
        group["total"] += float(candidate.get("probability") or 0)

    total_passes = max(1, len(passes))
    merged = [
        g["lead"] | {
            "probability": round(g["total"] / total_passes, 3),
            "votes": len(g["passes"]),
            "passes": total_passes,
        }
        for g in groups
    ]  # fmt: skip
    merged.sort(key=lambda c: (-c["votes"], -c["probability"]))

    return merged[:keep]


# ---- the sun -----------------------------------------------------------------------


def ring_zone(
    centre: tuple[float, float], angular_radius_deg: float, width_deg: float, label: str
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Every point a fixed angle from ``centre``: where a body stood at a given height."""
    return {
        "kind": "ring",
        "lat": round(centre[0], 4),
        "lon": round(centre[1], 4),
        "radius_km": round(max(0.0, angular_radius_deg) * _KM_PER_DEG, 1),
        "width_km": round(width_deg * _KM_PER_DEG, 1),
        "label": label,
    }


def band_zone(lat_min: float, lat_max: float, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "kind": "band",
        "lat_min": round(max(-90.0, lat_min), 2),
        "lat_max": round(min(90.0, lat_max), 2),
        "label": label,
    }


def in_ring(point: tuple[float, float], zone: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    apart = haversine_km(point, (zone["lat"], zone["lon"]))

    return abs(apart - zone["radius_km"]) <= zone["width_km"] / 2


def sun_ring(when: datetime, elevation_deg: float, tolerance_deg: float = 8.0) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Where the sun stood ``elevation_deg`` high at ``when``: a ring around the sub-solar point."""
    from earwitness.modules.provenance import subsolar_point

    return ring_zone(
        subsolar_point(when),
        90.0 - elevation_deg,
        2 * tolerance_deg,
        f"Sun {elevation_deg:.0f}° high at {when.astimezone(timezone.utc):%H:%M} UTC",
    )


def sun_check(
    when: datetime, lat: float, lon: float, inv: dict[str, Any]
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Does the sun the frames show fit this place at this time?"""
    from earwitness.modules.provenance import sun_position

    expected, _ = sun_position(when, lat, lon)
    lighting = inv.get("lighting")
    seen = inv.get("sun_elevation_deg")

    if lighting == "night" and expected > 6:
        return {"ok": False, "text": f"night in the frames, but the sun was {expected:.0f}° up there"}

    if lighting == "day" and expected < -4:
        return {"ok": False, "text": f"daylight in the frames, but the sun was {-expected:.0f}° below the horizon there"}

    if isinstance(seen, (int, float)) and inv.get("sun_visible"):
        off = abs(expected - float(seen))

        if off <= 12:
            return {"ok": True, "text": f"sun {expected:.0f}° high there, frames suggest ~{seen:.0f}°"}

        if off > 20:
            return {"ok": False, "text": f"sun {expected:.0f}° high there, frames suggest ~{seen:.0f}°"}

        return {"ok": None, "text": f"sun {expected:.0f}° high there, frames suggest ~{seen:.0f}° (unclear)"}

    if lighting in ("day", "night", "twilight"):
        return {"ok": True, "text": f"{lighting} fits (sun {expected:.0f}° there)"}

    return None


# ---- stars -------------------------------------------------------------------------


def gmst_deg(when: datetime) -> float:
    """Greenwich mean sidereal time, degrees."""
    jd = when.astimezone(timezone.utc).timestamp() / 86400 + 2440587.5

    return (280.46061837 + 360.98564736629 * (jd - 2451545.0)) % 360


def star_zones(
    ra_deg: float, dec_deg: float, tilt_deg: float | None, when: datetime | None
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Where a camera could see a star field centred on (RA, Dec).

    Seen at altitude ``a``, the field centre is ``90 - a`` degrees from the
    zenith, so the observer's latitude is within that of the declination; with
    a time the sub-star point is known too, and the locus is a ring.
    """
    spread = 90.0 - (tilt_deg if tilt_deg is not None else 0.0)
    zones = [
        band_zone(
            dec_deg - spread,
            dec_deg + spread,
            f"Star field at declination {dec_deg:+.0f}° is visible only here",
        )
    ]

    if when is not None and tilt_deg is not None:
        lon = (ra_deg - gmst_deg(when) + 180) % 360 - 180
        zones.append(
            ring_zone((dec_deg, lon), spread, 30.0, f"Star field {tilt_deg:.0f}° up at {when:%H:%M} UTC")
        )

    return zones


async def astrometry_solve(path: str, key: str, client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> dict[str, float] | None:
    """Plate-solve a sky photo with nova.astrometry.net: centre RA/Dec and field radius."""
    base = "https://nova.astrometry.net/api"
    import json

    try:
        login = await client.post(f"{base}/login", data={"request-json": json.dumps({"apikey": key})})
        session = login.json().get("session")

        if not session:
            return None

        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            upload = await client.post(
                f"{base}/upload",
                data={"request-json": json.dumps(
                    {"session": session, "publicly_visible": "n", "allow_commercial_use": "n"}
                )},
                files={"file": ("sky.jpg", handle.read(), "image/jpeg")},
            )  # fmt: skip
        sub = upload.json().get("subid")

        if not sub:
            return None

        for _ in range(40):  # about three minutes
            await asyncio.sleep(4.5)
            jobs = [j for j in (await client.get(f"{base}/submissions/{sub}")).json().get("jobs", []) if j]

            if not jobs:
                continue

            status = (await client.get(f"{base}/jobs/{jobs[0]}")).json().get("status")

            if status == "failure":
                return None

            if status == "success":
                cal = (await client.get(f"{base}/jobs/{jobs[0]}/calibration")).json()

                return {"ra": float(cal["ra"]), "dec": float(cal["dec"]), "radius": float(cal.get("radius", 0))}
    except httpx.HTTPError, ValueError, KeyError, OSError:
        return None

    return None


# ---- ground-level photos -----------------------------------------------------------

_NOT_A_PHOTO = ("map", "logo", "coat of arms", "diagram", "plan ", "chart", "svg", "flag", "locator")


def commons_pick(geosearch: dict[str, Any], imageinfo: dict[str, Any], n: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Nearest photographs from a Commons geosearch plus imageinfo response."""
    hits = geosearch.get("query", {}).get("geosearch", [])
    pages = {p.get("title"): p for p in imageinfo.get("query", {}).get("pages", {}).values()}
    picked = []

    for hit in sorted(hits, key=lambda h: h.get("dist", 1e9)):
        title = hit.get("title", "")

        if any(word in title.lower() for word in _NOT_A_PHOTO):
            continue

        info = (pages.get(title, {}).get("imageinfo") or [{}])[0]

        if info.get("mime") != "image/jpeg" or not info.get("thumburl"):
            continue

        picked.append(
            {"title": title.removeprefix("File:"), "url": info.get("descriptionurl", ""),
             "thumb": info["thumburl"], "dist_m": round(float(hit.get("dist", 0)))}
        )  # fmt: skip

        if len(picked) >= n:
            break

    return picked


async def commons_photos(
    client: httpx.AsyncClient, lat: float, lon: float, radius_m: int, n: int = 2
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Geotagged photographs on Wikimedia Commons near a point (no key needed)."""
    api = "https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php"

    try:
        search = (
            await client.get(api, params={
                "action": "query", "list": "geosearch", "gscoord": f"{lat}|{lon}",
                "gsradius": max(100, min(10000, radius_m)), "gsnamespace": 6, "gslimit": 25, "format": "json",
            })
        ).json()  # fmt: skip
        titles = [h["title"] for h in search.get("query", {}).get("geosearch", [])][:25]

        if not titles:
            return []

        info = (
            await client.get(api, params={
                "action": "query", "titles": "|".join(titles), "prop": "imageinfo",
                "iiprop": "url|mime", "iiurlwidth": 768, "format": "json",
            })
        ).json()  # fmt: skip
    except httpx.HTTPError, ValueError, KeyError:
        return []

    return commons_pick(search, info, n)


def mapillary_pick(response: dict[str, Any], lat: float, lon: float, n: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    images = []

    for item in response.get("data", []):
        coords = (item.get("computed_geometry") or item.get("geometry") or {}).get("coordinates")

        if not coords or not item.get("thumb_1024_url"):
            continue

        images.append(
            {"id": item["id"], "thumb": item["thumb_1024_url"],
             "dist_m": round(haversine_km((lat, lon), (coords[1], coords[0])) * 1000),
             "url": f"https://www.mapillary.com/app/?pKey={item['id']}"}
        )  # fmt: skip

    images.sort(key=lambda i: i["dist_m"])
    # Spread out: skip images within 150 m of one already chosen.
    chosen: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    for image in images:
        if all(abs(image["dist_m"] - c["dist_m"]) > 150 for c in chosen):
            chosen.append(image)

        if len(chosen) >= n:
            break

    return chosen


async def mapillary_photos(
    client: httpx.AsyncClient, lat: float, lon: float, n: int = 2
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Street-level images near a point (needs MAPILLARY_TOKEN)."""
    token = os.environ.get("MAPILLARY_TOKEN")

    if not token:
        return []

    d = 0.01  # Mapillary caps the box at 0.01 square degrees

    try:
        response = await client.get(
            "https://graph.mapillary.com/images",
            params={
                "access_token": token, "fields": "id,thumb_1024_url,computed_geometry,geometry",
                "bbox": f"{lon - d / 2},{lat - d / 2},{lon + d / 2},{lat + d / 2}", "limit": 30,
            },
        )  # fmt: skip
        response.raise_for_status()

        return mapillary_pick(response.json(), lat, lon, n)
    except httpx.HTTPError, ValueError, KeyError:
        return []


async def download(client: httpx.AsyncClient, url: str, path: str) -> bool:
    try:
        response = await client.get(url)
    except httpx.HTTPError:
        return False

    if response.status_code != 200 or len(response.content) > 6_000_000:
        return False

    with open(path, "wb") as handle:
        handle.write(response.content)

    return cv2.imread(path) is not None


# ---- OpenStreetMap -----------------------------------------------------------------


def overpass_query(lat: float, lon: float, features: list[str]) -> str:
    parts = [
        f"{selector}(around:{FEATURES[f][1]},{lat:.5f},{lon:.5f});"
        for f in features
        if f in FEATURES
        for selector in FEATURES[f][0]
    ]

    return "[out:json][timeout:25];(" + "".join(parts) + ");out tags 500;"


def overpass_found(response: dict[str, Any], features: list[str]) -> dict[str, bool]:
    """Which of ``features`` appear among the elements Overpass returned."""
    found = dict.fromkeys(features, False)

    for element in response.get("elements", []):
        tags = element.get("tags", {})
        kind = element.get("type")

        for feature in features:
            for selector in FEATURES.get(feature, ([], 0))[0]:
                want_type = selector.split("[", 1)[0]
                pairs = [p.strip('"]').split('"="') for p in selector.split("[")[1:]]

                if want_type == kind and all(tags.get(k.strip('"')) == v for k, v in pairs):
                    found[feature] = True

    return found


async def osm_features(
    client: httpx.AsyncClient, lat: float, lon: float, features: list[str]
) -> dict[str, bool] | None:
    """Presence of each feature near the point, from OpenStreetMap (no key needed)."""
    features = [f for f in features if f in FEATURES]

    if not features:
        return None

    query = overpass_query(lat, lon, features)

    for server in ("https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter", "https://overpass.kumi.systems/api/interpreter"):
        try:
            response = await client.post(server, data={"data": query}, timeout=40)

            if response.status_code == 200:
                return overpass_found(response.json(), features)
        except httpx.HTTPError, ValueError:
            continue

    return None


def osm_checks(found: dict[str, bool]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    return [
        {
            "ok": present,
            "text": f"{_FEATURE_WORDS[f]} {'mapped nearby' if present else 'seen, but none mapped within ' + format(FEATURES[f][1] / 1000, 'g') + ' km'}",
        }
        for f, present in found.items()
    ]


# ---- terrain skyline ---------------------------------------------------------------

_TERRARIUM = "https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"
_DEM_ZOOM = 10


def frame_skyline(rgb: np.ndarray, width: int = 320) -> np.ndarray | None:
    """Row of the skyline in each column (fraction of the height), or None.

    Sky is bright, smooth and connected to the top edge; the skyline is where
    it ends. Columns whose top is not sky are NaN. Needs sky across most of
    the frame, or there is no skyline to compare.
    """
    scale = width / rgb.shape[1]
    small = cv2.resize(rgb, (width, max(8, round(rgb.shape[0] * scale))), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    h = small.shape[0]
    gray = cv2.GaussianBlur(cv2.cvtColor(small, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY), (5, 5), 0).astype(np.float32)
    grad = np.hypot(cv2.Sobel(gray, cv2.CV_32F, 1, 0), cv2.Sobel(gray, cv2.CV_32F, 0, 1))
    top = gray[: max(2, h // 10)]
    bright = gray >= max(60.0, float(np.percentile(top, 20)) - 35)
    smooth = grad < max(18.0, float(np.percentile(grad, 60)))
    mask = (bright & smooth).astype(np.uint8)
    mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8))
    count, labels = cv2.connectedComponents(mask)
    top_labels = {int(v) for v in labels[0] if v}

    if not top_labels:
        return None

    sky = np.isin(labels, list(top_labels))
    rows = np.full(width, np.nan)

    for x in range(width):
        column = sky[:, x]

        if not column[0]:
            continue

        ends = np.flatnonzero(~column)
        rows[x] = (ends[0] if ends.size else h) / h

    valid = np.isfinite(rows)

    if valid.mean() < 0.7 or np.nanmedian(rows) > 0.92 or np.nanmedian(rows) < 0.05:
        return None

    return rows


def skyline_angles(rows: np.ndarray, aspect: float, hfov_deg: float) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """(azimuth offset, elevation angle) in degrees for each skyline column."""
    width = rows.size
    f = (width / 2) / math.tan(math.radians(hfov_deg) / 2)
    x = np.arange(width) - width / 2 + 0.5
    y = (0.5 - rows) * width / aspect

    return np.degrees(np.arctan(x / f)), np.degrees(np.arctan(y / f))


def lonlat_to_pixel(lat: float, lon: float, zoom: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    n = 256 * 2**zoom
    x = (lon + 180) / 360 * n
    y = (1 - math.asinh(math.tan(math.radians(lat))) / math.pi) / 2 * n

    return x, y


def decode_terrarium(png: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Terrarium tile (BGR as cv2 reads it) to metres."""
    b, g, r = (png[..., i].astype(np.float64) for i in range(3))

    return r * 256 + g + b / 256 - 32768


async def dem_around(
    client: httpx.AsyncClient, lat: float, lon: float, tiles: int = 3
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, float, float, float] | None:
    """Elevation mosaic around a point: (metres, x, y of the point, metres per pixel)."""
    px, py = lonlat_to_pixel(lat, lon, _DEM_ZOOM)
    tx, ty = int(px // 256), int(py // 256)
    half = tiles // 2
    mosaic = np.zeros((256 * tiles, 256 * tiles))

    async def tile(dx: int, dy: int) -> bool:
        url = _TERRARIUM.format(z=_DEM_ZOOM, x=(tx + dx) % (2**_DEM_ZOOM), y=ty + dy)

        try:
            response = await client.get(url)
        except httpx.HTTPError:
            return False

        image = cv2.imdecode(np.frombuffer(response.content, np.uint8), cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)

        if response.status_code != 200 or image is None:
            return False

        mosaic[(dy + half) * 256 : (dy + half + 1) * 256, (dx + half) * 256 : (dx + half + 1) * 256] = (
            decode_terrarium(image)
        )

        return True

    results = await asyncio.gather(*(tile(dx, dy) for dy in range(-half, half + 1) for dx in range(-half, half + 1)))

    if not all(results):
        return None

    metres = 156543.03392 * math.cos(math.radians(lat)) / 2**_DEM_ZOOM

    return mosaic, px - (tx - half) * 256, py - (ty - half) * 256, metres


def horizon_profile(
    dem: np.ndarray, x: float, y: float, metres_per_px: float, eye_m: float = 1.7, reach_m: float = 20000
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Elevation angle of the skyline in each whole-degree azimuth (0 = north, clockwise)."""
    azimuth = np.radians(np.arange(360))[:, None]
    reach = min(reach_m, metres_per_px * (min(dem.shape) / 2 - 2))
    distance = np.geomspace(60.0, reach, 220)[None, :]
    sx = np.clip(np.round(x + np.sin(azimuth) * distance / metres_per_px), 0, dem.shape[1] - 1).astype(int)
    sy = np.clip(np.round(y - np.cos(azimuth) * distance / metres_per_px), 0, dem.shape[0] - 1).astype(int)
    ground = dem[int(round(y)), int(round(x))] + eye_m
    # Earth curvature less refraction (k = 0.13) lowers distant ground.
    drop = distance**2 / (2 * EARTH_KM * 1000) * 0.87
    angles = np.degrees(np.arctan2(dem[sy, sx] - ground - drop, distance))

    return angles.max(axis=1)


def match_skyline(
    rows: np.ndarray, aspect: float, profile: np.ndarray, fovs: tuple[float, ...] = (55.0, 69.0, 80.0)
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Best correlation of the frame's skyline with the rendered horizon over headings and FOVs.

    Camera pitch is unknown, so both curves are compared with their means
    removed: the shape of the skyline, not its height in the frame, is matched.
    """
    best: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    valid = np.isfinite(rows)

    for fov in fovs:
        offsets, seen = skyline_angles(rows, aspect, fov)
        offsets, seen = offsets[valid], seen[valid]
        seen_c = seen - seen.mean()

        if seen_c.std() < 0.25:
            return {"score": None, "relief_seen": float(np.ptp(seen)), "relief_there": float(np.ptp(profile))}

        for heading in range(360):
            there = np.interp((heading + offsets) % 360, np.arange(361), np.append(profile, profile[0]))
            there_c = there - there.mean()

            if there_c.std() < 1e-6:
                continue

            r = float(np.dot(seen_c, there_c) / (np.linalg.norm(seen_c) * np.linalg.norm(there_c)))
            ratio = there_c.std() / seen_c.std()
            score = r if 0.4 <= ratio <= 2.5 else r * 0.5

            if best is None or score > best["score"]:
                best = {
                    "score": round(score, 3), "heading": heading, "fov": fov,
                    "relief_seen": round(float(np.ptp(seen)), 2), "relief_there": round(float(np.ptp(there)), 2),
                }  # fmt: skip

    return best


async def skyline_check(
    client: httpx.AsyncClient, rows: np.ndarray, aspect: float, lat: float, lon: float
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Compare the frame's skyline with the terrain at and around the candidate."""
    dem = await dem_around(client, lat, lon)

    if dem is None:
        return None

    mosaic, x, y, metres = dem
    best = None
    step = 1500 / metres  # also try 1.5 km around: the candidate is only approximate

    for dx, dy in ((0, 0), (step, 0), (-step, 0), (0, step), (0, -step)):
        profile = horizon_profile(mosaic, x + dx, y + dy, metres)
        result = await asyncio.to_thread(match_skyline, rows, aspect, profile)

        if result and result.get("score") is not None and (best is None or result["score"] > best["score"]):
            best = result | {"profile": [round(float(v), 2) for v in profile]}

    if best is None:
        return None

    if best["relief_there"] < 0.4 and best["relief_seen"] >= 1.5:
        return best | {"ok": False, "text": f"hills on the skyline, but the land there is flat ({best['relief_there']:.1f}° of relief)"}

    if best["score"] >= 0.85:
        return best | {"ok": True, "text": f"skyline matches the terrain ({best['score'] * 100:.0f}%, looking {_compass(best['heading'])})"}

    return best | {"ok": None, "text": f"skyline match {best['score'] * 100:.0f}% (inconclusive: trees and buildings hide the terrain)"}


def _compass(heading: float) -> str:
    names = ["north", "north-east", "east", "south-east", "south", "south-west", "west", "north-west"]

    return names[round(heading / 45) % 8]


# ---- weather -----------------------------------------------------------------------


async def weather_check(lat: float, lon: float, when: datetime, seen: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    from earwitness.modules import weather

    wet_seen, dry_seen = weather._seen_conditions(seen)

    if not (wet_seen or dry_seen):
        return None

    record = await weather._hourly(lat, lon, when)

    if record is None:
        return None

    sky = weather._CODES.get(int(record.get("weather_code") or 0), "unknown")
    rain = float(record.get("precipitation") or 0)
    wet = rain >= 0.5 or sky.endswith(("rain", "drizzle", "showers"))
    dry = rain == 0 and int(record.get("weather_code") or 0) <= 2

    if (wet and dry_seen) or (dry and wet_seen):
        return {"ok": False, "text": f"weather there was {sky}, the frames look {'dry' if dry_seen else 'wet'}"}

    return {"ok": True, "text": f"weather there was {sky}, which fits"}

    main = os.environ.get("EARWITNESS_GRID_SEED_SCHEMA", "earwitness")

    async with db.connection() as conn:
        present = await (
            await conn.execute(
                "SELECT to_regclass(%s) IS NOT NULL", [f"{main}.grid_coverage"]
            )
        ).fetchone()

        if not present[0]:
            return

        await conn.execute(
            sql.SQL(
                "INSERT INTO grid_frequency SELECT * FROM {}.grid_frequency"
                " ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING"
            ).format(sql.Identifier(main))
        )
        await conn.execute(
            sql.SQL("INSERT INTO grid_coverage SELECT * FROM {}.grid_coverage").format(
                sql.Identifier(main)
            )
        )

"""Effort levels: recorded per case, changeable on rerun, and gating modules."""

import asyncio

import cv2
import numpy as np
import pytest
from test_auth import ALICE  # noqa: F401 - fixtures below are used by name
from test_auth import bearer
from test_auth import client  # noqa: F401
from test_auth import owned_case
from test_auth import profiles  # noqa: F401
from test_auth import token

from earwitness.modules import registry
from earwitness.modules.base import CaseContext
from earwitness.server import app as server
from earwitness.server import jobs


def test_bad_effort_is_refused_before_a_case_exists(client):  # noqa: F811
    before = len(server.store.cases)
    response = client.post(
        "/api/cases?effort=extreme",
        files={"file": ("clip.mp4", b"not a video")},
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token()}"},
    )

    assert response.status_code == 400
    assert len(server.store.cases) == before


def test_rerun_changes_and_records_the_effort(client, profiles, monkeypatch):  # noqa: F811
    case = owned_case(ALICE)
    restarted = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(server.store, "restart", lambda c, only=None: restarted.append(c.id))

    assert client.post(f"/api/cases/{case.id}/rerun?effort=fast", headers=bearer(ALICE)).status_code == 400

    response = client.post(f"/api/cases/{case.id}/rerun?effort=high", headers=bearer(ALICE))

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["effort"] == "high"
    assert case.options["effort"] == "high"
    assert case.history[-1]["action"] == "reran" and case.history[-1]["effort"] == "high"
    assert restarted == [case.id]

    # Saved to case.json, so it survives a restart of the server.
    open(case.evidence_path, "wb").close()
    assert type(server.store)(server.store.root).cases[case.id].options["effort"] == "high"


def test_cases_without_an_effort_are_standard(client, profiles):  # noqa: F811
    case = owned_case(ALICE)

    assert case.summary()["effort"] == "medium"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "options, effort, picked",
    [({}, "medium", 6), ({"effort": "low"}, "low", 3), ({"effort": "high"}, "high", 10), ({"effort": "silly"}, "medium", 6)],
)
def test_by_effort(options, effort, picked):
    ctx = CaseContext("t", "/nonexistent.mp4", "/tmp", options)

    assert ctx.effort == effort
    assert ctx.by_effort(low=3, medium=6, high=10) == picked
    # A level left out falls back to the medium value.
    assert ctx.by_effort(low="low") == ("low" if effort == "low" else None)


class _DeepOnly:
    name = "deep_only"
    title = "DEEP"
    description = "runs only at high effort"
    min_effort = "high"

    async def run(self, ctx, out):
        ctx.publish(self.name, "ran")


class _Waiter:
    name = "waiter"
    title = "WAITER"
    description = "waits on deep_only"

    async def run(self, ctx, out):
        out.finding("info", f"deep_only said {await ctx.wait_for('deep_only', 5)!r}", "")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("effort, said, status", [("medium", "None", "skipped"), ("high", "'ran'", "done")])
def test_min_effort_skips_without_blocking_others(tmp_path, monkeypatch, effort, said, status):
    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "all_modules", lambda kind="video": [_DeepOnly(), _Waiter()])
    store = jobs.CaseStore(str(tmp_path))
    case = store.create("still.png", {"effort": effort})
    cv2.imwrite(case.evidence_path, np.full((32, 48, 3), 128, np.uint8))

    asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(jobs.run_case(case), 60))

    statuses = {e["module"]: e["status"] for e in case.events if e["type"] == "module"}
    assert statuses["deep_only"] == status
    assert statuses["waiter"] == "done"
    assert [e["finding"]["title"] for e in case.events if e["type"] == "finding"] == [f"deep_only said {said}"]
    assert next(e for e in case.events if e["type"] == "case")["case"]["effort"] == effort

"""Deep geolocation helpers: the maths and the parsing, without the network."""

from datetime import datetime
from datetime import timezone

import numpy as np

from earwitness.modules import geo_deep as g
from earwitness.modules.provenance import sun_position
from earwitness.modules.provenance import subsolar_point

EDINBURGH = (55.95, -3.19)


def test_subsolar_point_has_the_sun_overhead():
    for when in (datetime(2026, 6, 21, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc), datetime(2026, 11, 8, 15, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc)):
        lat, lon = subsolar_point(when)

        assert sun_position(when, lat, lon)[0] > 89.5


def test_sun_ring_passes_through_the_true_place():
    when = datetime(2026, 8, 1, 13, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    elevation, _ = sun_position(when, *EDINBURGH)
    ring = g.sun_ring(when, elevation)

    assert g.in_ring(EDINBURGH, ring)
    # Sydney saw no such sun at that moment.
    assert not g.in_ring((-33.87, 151.21), ring)


def test_sun_check_catches_night_against_a_high_sun():
    when = datetime(2026, 8, 1, 13, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

    assert g.sun_check(when, *EDINBURGH, {"lighting": "night"})["ok"] is False
    assert g.sun_check(when, *EDINBURGH, {"lighting": "day", "sun_visible": True, "sun_elevation_deg": 48})["ok"] is True


def test_star_band_bounds_the_latitude():
    # A field near the south celestial pole cannot be seen from Edinburgh.
    band = g.star_zones(200.0, -60.0, None, None)[0]

    assert band["lat_max"] == 30.0 and band["lat_min"] == -90.0


def test_cluster_counts_agreeing_passes():
    a = {"place": "Peebles", "latitude": 55.65, "longitude": -3.19, "probability": 0.5}
    b = {"place": "near Peebles", "latitude": 55.70, "longitude": -3.25, "probability": 0.3}
    c = {"place": "Keswick", "latitude": 54.60, "longitude": -3.13, "probability": 0.4}

    merged = g.cluster([[a, c], [b], [dict(a, probability=0.2)]])

    assert merged[0]["place"] == "Peebles"
    assert merged[0]["votes"] == 3 and merged[0]["passes"] == 3
    assert merged[0]["probability"] == round((0.5 + 0.3 + 0.2) / 3, 3)
    assert merged[1]["place"] == "Keswick" and merged[1]["votes"] == 1


def test_overpass_found_matches_tags():
    response = {
        "elements": [
            {"type": "node", "tags": {"power": "generator", "generator:source": "wind"}},
            {"type": "way", "tags": {"natural": "coastline"}},
            {"type": "node", "tags": {"natural": "coastline"}},  # wrong element type
        ]
    }

    found = g.overpass_found(response, ["wind_turbine", "coastline", "railway"])

    assert found == {"wind_turbine": True, "coastline": True, "railway": False}
    assert "around:12000" in g.overpass_query(55.0, -3.0, ["wind_turbine"])
    assert [c["ok"] for c in g.osm_checks(found)] == [True, True, False]


def test_commons_pick_skips_maps_and_non_photos():
    search = {"query": {"geosearch": [
        {"title": "File:Location map of Peebles.jpg", "dist": 10},
        {"title": "File:Track over the moor.jpg", "dist": 300},
        {"title": "File:Drawing.svg", "dist": 50},
    ]}}  # fmt: skip
    info = {"query": {"pages": {
        "1": {"title": "File:Location map of Peebles.jpg", "imageinfo": [{"mime": "image/jpeg", "thumburl": "u1"}]},
        "2": {"title": "File:Track over the moor.jpg", "imageinfo": [{"mime": "image/jpeg", "thumburl": "u2", "descriptionurl": "d2"}]},
        "3": {"title": "File:Drawing.svg", "imageinfo": [{"mime": "image/svg+xml", "thumburl": "u3"}]},
    }}}  # fmt: skip

    assert g.commons_pick(search, info, 2) == [
        {"title": "Track over the moor.jpg", "url": "d2", "thumb": "u2", "dist_m": 300}
    ]


def test_mapillary_pick_spreads_out():
    response = {"data": [
        {"id": "1", "thumb_1024_url": "a", "computed_geometry": {"coordinates": [-3.19, 55.9501]}},
        {"id": "2", "thumb_1024_url": "b", "computed_geometry": {"coordinates": [-3.19, 55.9502]}},
        {"id": "3", "thumb_1024_url": "c", "computed_geometry": {"coordinates": [-3.19, 55.9540]}},
    ]}  # fmt: skip

    assert [i["id"] for i in g.mapillary_pick(response, *EDINBURGH, 2)] == ["1", "3"]


def _ridge_dem() -> np.ndarray:
    """Flat ground with a 600 m ridge 5 km to the north."""
    dem = np.zeros((400, 400))
    dem[130:140, :] = 600.0  # 100 m per pixel: rows 130-140 are ~6 km north of row 200

    return dem


def test_horizon_profile_sees_the_ridge_to_the_north():
    profile = g.horizon_profile(_ridge_dem(), 200, 200, 100.0)

    assert profile[0] > 4  # atan(600 / ~6500 m) is about 5 degrees
    assert abs(profile[180]) < 0.5
    assert profile.argmax() in (0, 359, 1)


def test_skyline_from_frame_and_match():
    profile = g.horizon_profile(_ridge_dem(), 200, 200, 100.0) + np.sin(np.radians(np.arange(360)) * 6) * 2
    w, h = 400, 300
    offsets, _ = g.skyline_angles(np.zeros(w), w / h, 69.0)
    there = np.interp((30 + offsets) % 360, np.arange(361), np.append(profile, profile[0]))
    f = (w / 2) / np.tan(np.radians(69.0) / 2)
    rows = 0.5 - np.tan(np.radians(there - there.mean())) * f / h
    image = np.full((h, w, 3), (80, 100, 50), np.uint8)

    for x in range(w):
        image[: int(rows[x] * h), x] = (175, 205, 240)

    seen = g.frame_skyline(image, width=w)

    assert seen is not None and np.isfinite(seen).mean() > 0.95

    best = g.match_skyline(seen, w / h, profile)

    assert best["score"] > 0.95
    assert abs(best["heading"] - 30) <= 2


def test_frame_without_sky_has_no_skyline():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)

    assert g.frame_skyline(rng.integers(0, 255, (240, 320, 3), dtype=np.uint8)) is None


def test_inventory_text_drops_empty_fields():
    text = g.inventory_text({"road": "single track, no lines", "vehicles": "none", "hemisphere_hint": "unknown",
                             "strongest_clues": ["dry-stone walls"]})  # fmt: skip

    assert "Road: single track" in text
    assert "Vehicles" not in text and "Hemisphere" not in text
    assert "dry-stone walls" in text

content.text:
I've built the Effort setting (Quick / Standard / Deep) and all the Deep methods from the plan, but nothing is committed or deployed yet. The new code passes its tests with the AI mocked out; it hasn't yet run with a real AI model. The full test suite passes (92 passed, 1 skipped), lint and the web build are clean, and I checked the new screens in the preview.

**How the effort setting works**
- **Choosing it:** the home page has Quick / Standard / Deep tabs above the dropzone, with rough times. On a case page there's a dropdown next to the AI picker for reruns.
- **Recording it:** each case stores its effort, and each upload or rerun entry in the case history notes the level used. Quick and Deep cases show a badge in the header and on the case card.
- **Standard** is unchanged.
- **Quick** looks at 3 frames instead of 6, skips the zoomed edge-crop step and the pulse check, and has the AI reason briefly. I kept the Wikipedia photo lookup rather than "satellite only" as planned, because it adds no wait.

**What Deep adds, aimed at countryside with no text**
- **Clue inventory:** before guessing, the AI lists rural clues: poles, road lines, walls, crops, soil, terrain, skyline, sun, shadows and stars.
- **Three independent guesses:** three passes on different frames; places they agree on rank higher ("3 of 3 independent passes agree").
- **Photos taken nearby:** Wikimedia Commons, which in the UK includes a lot of countryside photos. Mapillary street-level photos are also wired in once there's a token.
- **OpenStreetMap:** checks that things seen in the frame (wind turbines, pylons, coast, railway) exist near each candidate.
- **Terrain skyline:** compares the skyline in the frame with the horizon worked out from elevation data at each candidate, so "hills here, flat land there" counts against a place.
- **Sun:** when the capture time can be trusted, the sun's height puts the camera on a ring drawn in yellow on the map, and each candidate is checked against it.
- **Stars:** a star field limits which latitudes the photo could be from. This needs an astrometry.net key.
- **Weather:** recorded weather at each candidate is compared with what the frames show.
- **Zoom-in round:** if the answer is only regional, the AI looks again at satellite views of that region for the exact spot.
- **Ruling places out:** two or more failed checks stop a candidate from counting as verified.
- **Where you see it:** a new "Deep checks" tab in the location panel shows each candidate's checks.

Screenshots and files without metadata still run every Deep method. Only the steps that need a capture time (sun ring, weather) are skipped, and the finding says so.

**Possible bug on prod:** Wikimedia rejected our old User-Agent string with a 403 when I fetched a photo's details. The existing Wikipedia landmark-photo lookup used the same string, so it may have been quietly failing. I haven't checked prod cases for this. The fix (adding a contact URL) is included.

**Untested:**
- Mapillary and astrometry.net, because there are no keys yet.
- A real Deep run. This needs a deploy, then rerunning the two rural cases (the lane near Würzburg and the moor south of Edinburgh) at Deep and comparing the error with their Standard runs.
- **Cost:** Deep makes about 7–8 high-effort AI calls per case instead of 2.

**Keys to register** (both free and optional, and each step skips with a note without its key):
1. **Mapillary:** a client token from mapillary.com/dashboard/developers, set as `MAPILLARY_TOKEN`. Most useful for rural verification.
2. **astrometry.net:** an API key from nova.astrometry.net, set as `ASTROMETRY_API_KEY`. For night skies.

Say "commit push deploy" and I'll ship it and rerun the two rural cases at Deep.
Mapillary was already set in .env, nova.astronometry.net login is actually broken, is it possible to replace it?

t = tetra3.Tetra3()  # loads default_database.npz
st = t.star_table  # columns: ra, dec, x, y, z, mag (radians)
ra0, dec0, fov, w, h = np.radians(83.8), np.radians(-5.4), 24.0, 1000, 750  # Orion
c = np.array([np.cos(dec0)*np.cos(ra0), np.cos(dec0)*np.sin(ra0), np.sin(dec0)])
east = np.array([-np.sin(ra0), np.cos(ra0), 0]); north = np.cross(c, east)
v = st[:, 2:5]; dot = v @ c
f = (w/2)/np.tan(np.radians(fov)/2)
keep = dot > np.cos(np.radians(fov))
px = w/2 + f*(v[keep] @ east)/dot[keep]; py = h/2 - f*(v[keep] @ north)/dot[keep]; mag = st[keep, 5]
img = np.random.default_rng(0).normal(12, 3, (h, w))
yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w]
for x, y, m in zip(px, py, mag):
    if 0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h and m < 6.5:
        a = 255 * 10 ** (-0.4 * (m - 1))
        x0, y0 = int(x), int(y)
        sl = (slice(max(0,y0-6), y0+7), slice(max(0,x0-6), x0+7))
        img[sl] += min(a, 240) * np.exp(-((xx[sl]-x)**2 + (yy[sl]-y)**2) / 3.0)
im = Image.fromarray(np.clip(img, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8))
t0 = time.time()
r = t.solve_from_image(im, fov_estimate=fov, fov_max_error=8)
print(round(time.time()-t0, 2), "s", {k: r.get(k) for k in ("RA", "Dec", "FOV", "Roll", "Matches", "Prob")})

def load_database(self, path='default_database'):
